1: # Kanban Task Board
2: 
3: ## Overview
4: 
5: A **Kanban Task Board** is a work-management application whose world is a visual board: work is represented as cards, cards are held in ordered columns, and a card's position on the board is the record of where that work stands. Moving a card from column to column is how progress happens and how progress is seen.
6: 
7: The defining core is small:
8: 
9: ```text
10: Board (the organizing surface: ordered columns)
11: └── Card (the unit of work)
12:     └── Position-as-state (column membership = the card's status;
13:         moving the card = the state change; column order = progression
14:         toward done; card order = sequence/priority)
15: ```
16: 
17: Everything else the market associates with the category — card details, team collaboration, WIP limits, swimlanes, templates, automation, analytics, extra views — is standard or optional structure layered on that core, not what defines it. The software's ancestry is a physical whiteboard or wall with card notes; the product persists, shares, and scales that grammar. When the primary working model shifts away from the board — to a flat checklist, to task records with status fields viewed in lists, or to an ordered backlog driving timeboxed delivery — the product has crossed into a neighboring Application Type.
18: 
19: ## Users & Context
20: 
21: Two user populations share one structure:
22: 
23: - **Individuals** use a board as a personal work surface: a private to-do flow (to-do → doing → done), a plan being assembled, a small project. A single-user board is a first-class form, not a degenerate case.
24: - **Team members** work from a shared board that mirrors the team's own process. Members move cards as they take up and finish work; the board is the team's shared picture of who is doing what.
25: - **Stakeholders and managers** largely read the board rather than operate it: status at a glance, where work is piling up, what is blocked or aging.
26: 
27: The typical context is an ongoing flow of work rather than a fixed plan: requests and tasks arrive, get taken up, move through a few recognizable stages, and complete. Boards serve many settings — product and engineering teams, marketing and operations, sales processes, personal productivity — because the columns are defined by the users, not by the product.
28: 
29: ## Core Model
30: 
31: ### The Defining Core
32: 
33: **The board.** The board is the primary working surface and the model of record — not one view over some other task database. A board usually frames one process, team, project, or purpose. It is divided into vertical **columns**, arranged left to right in the order the users' process unfolds.
34: 
35: **The column (list / stage).** A named container for cards at the same point of the process. Column names come from the users' own workflow — backlog-ish, in-progress-ish, review-ish, done-ish — and are freely configurable: renamed, added, reordered, split. Column membership is meaningful: it is where the work stands. Columns may be subdivided into sub-columns for finer steps, and may carry capacity rules (see WIP limits under standard capabilities). Horizontal rows — **swimlanes** — can cross-cut the columns to separate types of work or classes of service.
36: 
37: **The card.** A self-contained unit of work: a task, request, deliverable, or item to handle. A card carries its own details on its face and inside — title, description, assignee or members, due date, labels or colors, attachments, checklists, comments, and a history of what happened to it. Cards are movable; that movability is the point.
38: 
39: **Position as state.** The card's column membership is the status. There is no separate status field that must be kept in sync: to change the state of the work, you move the card. Column order expresses progression from not-started toward done; the order of cards within a column expresses sequence or priority. A completed card either rests in a done column, gets marked complete, or is moved to an archive — the board's terminal handling keeps finished work out of the way without destroying it.
40: 
41: ### Concept and Implementation
42: 
43: The core is written conceptually; products realize it with different vocabularies:
44: 
45: ```text
46: Concept:   Board        → implementations:  board, project board, workflow board
47: Concept:   Column       → implementations:  list, lane stage, workflow state column,
48:                                             sub-columns for finer steps
49: Concept:   Card         → implementations:  card, task card, work item card
50: Concept:   Position     → implementations:  column membership (+ optional completion
51:             as state                       flag, archive move, in-column ordering)
52: ```
53: 
54: A reader who has only seen one product's vocabulary should still recognize any other board tool from this model.
55: 
56: ### Standard Capabilities
57: 
58: Mature products almost universally add:
59: 
60: - **Card detail** — description, assignee/members, due dates, labels or colors, attachments, checklists/subtasks, comments with notifications, per-card activity history.
61: - **Real-time collaboration** — several people working the same board with live updates.
62: - **Board membership and permissions** — who can see or edit a board; role tiers on larger accounts; per-board access levels.
63: - **Workflow customization** — rename/add/reorder columns, sub-columns, collapsible columns and swimlanes, board backgrounds.
64: - **Search and filtering** — find cards across the board (and the archive) by text, member, label, date.
65: - **Board templates and cloning** — start from a prebuilt flow (task tracking, sales pipeline, product development) or duplicate an existing board.
66: - **Automation** — rules that move, label, or otherwise act on cards when triggers occur (e.g., "when a card moves to review, assign a reviewer").
67: - **Archiving** — completed cards leave the board but remain searchable.
68: - **Notifications** — assignments, mentions, and due-date reminders, typically via email or in-app.
69: - **API, integrations, and mobile clients.**
70: 
71: ### Optional / Segment-dependent Capabilities
72: 
73: - **WIP limits** — a cap per column on how many cards it may hold, so the team finishes started work before pulling more. Method-standard for kanban practice and prominent in methodology-first products; not present natively in every general-purpose tool.
74: - **Swimlanes** — present in many team-oriented products, absent from the simplest forms.
75: - **Flow analytics** — cumulative flow diagrams, cycle/lead time, aging, forecasting from historical data. The signature of methodology-first and enterprise offerings.
76: - **Time tracking** — timers and reports attached to cards (a differentiator of some products rather than the norm).
77: - **Secondary views** — calendar, timeline, table, or dashboard renderings of the same cards.
78: - **Cross-board machinery** — moving cards between boards, linked board networks, portfolio layers above boards in enterprise suites.
79: - **AI assistance** — text drafting, board construction from a description, or agents that execute cards on the board (current-generation layer).
80: 
81: ## How It Works
82: 
83: ### Shape the board
84: 
85: ```text
86: Create a board
87: → name the columns after the real process (often starting from a template:
88:    "to do / doing / done", or a richer request → in progress → review → done)
89: → optionally split columns, add swimlanes, set WIP limits
90: → invite members, set who can view/edit
91: ```
92: 
93: The board is configured, not programmed. As the process changes, the columns change — the same vendor guidance everywhere: the board should mirror how the team actually works.
94: 
95: ### Fill and work the flow
96: 
97: ```text
98: Cards enter the board (added by hand, captured from requests/integrations,
99:    or imported in bulk)
100: → a member picks up a card (usually from the top of the first column)
101: → moves it into the working column
102: → does the work; discusses and attaches material on the card
103: → moves it onward through review/delivery stages
104: → it reaches done and is archived or left to rest
105: ```
106: 
107: This is a pull loop: people take up work as they free themselves, ideally finishing what they have before starting more. Where WIP limits are configured, the overfilled column becomes visible as a stop signal; how strictly the software enforces the cap varies by product. Dragging the card is not decoration — it *is* the status update, performed by the person doing the work, which is why the board can stay current without a reporting ceremony.
108: 
109: ### Steer by looking
110: 
111: The board is designed to be read at a distance: a glance shows what is on deck, what is in motion, what is done, and where cards accumulate. Teams use it in their regular check-ins; bottlenecks show up as fat columns, stalled or blocked work as aging cards, and overload as columns pressed against their limits. Managers and stakeholders read the same surface instead of asking for status.
112: 
113: ### Adjust over time
114: 
115: Boards are living structures: columns get renamed, merged, or sliced as the process is refined; cards get moved between boards; finished boards are archived. The improvement loop — look at flow, change the board, work the new flow — is part of the product's normal operation.
116: 
117: ### Defining core vs standard vs optional
118: 
119: - **Defining core** — board, cards, position-as-state, movement as the state change.
120: - **Standard capabilities** — card detail, real-time collaboration, permissions, workflow customization, search/filter, templates, automation, archive, notifications, API/mobile.
121: - **Optional / variant** — WIP limits, swimlanes, flow analytics, time tracking, secondary views, cross-board linking, AI, deployment choices, personal vs team orientation.
122: 
123: ## Interfaces
124: 
125: ### The board surface
126: 
127: The product's main screen.
128: 
129: - shows the board: columns left to right, swimlanes across, cards stacked in each column
130: - cards display a summary face (title, colors/labels, members, due date, checklist progress)
131: - primary actions: add a card, drag a card within or across columns, filter/search, open a card, collapse areas, open the board menu
132: 
133: ### Card detail view
134: 
135: Opens from any card.
136: 
137: - description, checklist with progress, members, dates, labels, attachments, comments, activity history
138: - primary actions: edit details, assign, comment, attach, move (or drag from here), copy/move to another board, archive or delete
139: 
140: ### Board menu / settings
141: 
142: The board's control panel.
143: 
144: - members and permissions, background and appearance, automation rules, power-ups/extensions, activity feed, archive access
145: - primary actions: manage access, configure the workflow (columns, swimlanes, WIP limits), set up automations, search the board
146: 
147: ### Boards home / switcher
148: 
149: The entry surface listing a user's boards and available templates.
150: 
151: - board previews, favorites, team/workspace groupings, template gallery
152: - primary actions: create a board, start from a template, open a recent board
153: 
154: ### Secondary surfaces (where offered)
155: 
156: Calendar, timeline, table, or dashboard renderings of the same cards; analytics screens (cumulative flow, cycle time, aging) in methodology-oriented products.
157: 
158: ## Important Rules / Behaviors
159: 
160: - **Position is the status.** The card's column membership is the authoritative state of the work. There is no second status field to reconcile; the board cannot lie about where work stands unless someone fails to move a card.
161: - **The workflow is user-defined.** The product fixes no particular set of stages. Column names, count, and meaning are the users' own; two boards in the same product can model entirely different processes.
162: - **Movement is the update operation.** Dragging a card between columns — with the position confirmed in the card's history — is how state changes are made; some products let rules automate specific moves.
163: - **Capacity rules bind when configured.** A WIP limit makes an overfull column visually (and sometimes mechanically) resist new cards. The pull discipline — finish before starting more — is a practice the board supports, not one software generally enforces.
164: - **Card order carries sequence.** Within a column, top-to-bottom order serves as the working priority, and members commonly take up cards from the top.
165: - **Terminal work is preserved, not erased.** Completion moves cards to a done state or an archive; history remains inspectable, and the archive is searchable.
166: - **Access is scoped per board.** A board has its own member/permission scope; boards can be private, team-shared, or broadly visible depending on the product's model.
167: - **Boards are cheap to create and disposable by design.** One process or purpose per board; proliferation is expected and handled with a home/switcher surface.
168: 
169: ## Variants
170: 
171: - **Personal kanban boards** — single-user boards for private to-dos and planning; the simplest full form of the Type.
172: - **Team process boards** — shared boards with permissions, swimlanes, and automation; the center of gravity of the market.
173: - **General-purpose board-first tools** — the archetype: any workflow, any purpose, boards as the whole product.
174: - **Methodology-first products** — lean/kanban-practice tools that foreground WIP limits, explicit policies, and flow metrics.
175: - **Boards as a module** — board functionality embedded in task-management, workspace, or project-portfolio suites; the board's own model is unchanged by the packaging.
176: - **Enterprise deployments** — linked board networks, portfolio layers above boards, enterprise access governance.
177: - **Deployment forms** — cloud service, self-hosted commercial, open-source self-hosted.
178: - **Secondary board uses** — idea boards, information and resource hubs: the same surface applied where the "flow" degenerates to loose categories.
179: 
180: ## Related Application Types
181: 
182: | Application Type | Distinction |
183: |---|---|
184: | To-do List Application | centers on a flat checklist with completion ticks and reminders; no board grammar — remove the columns and position-as-state and this Type collapses into it |
185: | Task Management Application | centers on task *records* with status fields, priority, and list/calendar views; a kanban board there is one projection view over the records, whereas here the board is the native model and position is the state of record — the sharpest seam in this cluster |
186: | Agile Project Management Application | the board is one surface of that Type; its defining structure adds a team-owned ordered backlog, a bounded delivery cadence (timeboxed iteration or continuous pull) as the re-planning boundary, and feedback metrics — none of which belongs to this Type's core |
187: | Project Management Application | plan/schedule-centric: tasks with dates, dependencies, and resources measured against a plan; a board may be one of its views |
188: | Digital Whiteboard | a freeform spatial canvas with no card-state model; kanban templates on a whiteboard are optional task machinery, not this Type — remove position-as-state and allow free arrangement and it becomes a whiteboard |
189: | Issue Tracker / Bug Tracking System | centers on the issue record and its admin-defined workflow schema and reporting; boards are a common view rather than the model of record |
190: | Sales Pipeline Management | identical board grammar applied to a different world model (deals, buyers, values, win/loss) — sharing a surface grammar does not make one Type |
191: | Work Management / Team Workspace Platforms | broad containers that may include boards as one module; embedding is packaging, not Type identity |
192: 
193: The boundary worth remembering: the question is never "does the product have a kanban view?" but "is the board where the work state lives?" If the board is a rendering over a task table, the product belongs to task management; if the board is the record, it is a Kanban Task Board.
194: 
195: ## Representative Products
196: 
197: - Trello — general-purpose board-first archetype (personal free tier through enterprise)
198: - Kanban Tool — SMB/team pure-play with kanban-method emphasis and time tracking
199: - Businessmap (formerly Kanbanize) — enterprise lean platform carrying boards inside a portfolio/OKR suite
200: - Wekan — open-source, self-hosted board tool
201: 
202: The defining core was checked against the physical whiteboard antecedent and the open-source minimal form to avoid defining the Type by today's cloud-and-AI packaging.

Boards serve many settings — product and engineering teams, marketing and operations, sales processes, personal productivity — because the columns are defined by the users, not by the product.
28: 
29: ## Core Model
30: 
31: ### The Defining Core
32: 
33: **The board.** The board is the primary working surface and the model of record — not one view over some other task database. A board usually frames one process, team, project, or purpose. It is divided into vertical **columns**, arranged left to right in the order the users' process unfolds.
34: 
35: **The column (list / stage).** A named container for cards at the same point of the process. Column names come from the users' own workflow — backlog-ish, in-progress-ish, review-ish, done-ish — and are freely configurable: renamed, added, reordered, split. Column membership is meaningful: it is where the work stands. Columns may be subdivided into sub-columns for finer steps, and may carry capacity rules (see WIP limits under standard capabilities). Horizontal rows — **swimlanes** — can cross-cut the columns to separate types of work or classes of service.
36: 
37: **The card.** A self-contained unit of work: a task, request, deliverable, or item to handle. A card carries its own details on its face and inside — title, description, assignee or members, due date, labels or colors, attachments, checklists, comments, and a history of what happened to it. Cards are movable; that movability is the point.
38: 
39: **Position as state.** The card's column membership is the status. There is no separate status field that must be kept in sync: to change the state of the work, you move the card. Column order expresses progression from not-started toward done; the order of cards within a column expresses sequence or priority. A completed card either rests in a done column, gets marked complete, or is moved to an archive — the board's terminal handling keeps finished work out of the way without destroying it.
40: 
41: ### Concept and Implementation
42: 
43: The core is written conceptually; products realize it with different vocabularies:
44: 
45: ```text
46: Concept:   Board        → implementations:  board, project board, workflow board
47: Concept:   Column       → implementations:  list, lane stage, workflow state column,
48:                                             sub-columns for finer steps
49: Concept:   Card         → implementations:  card, task card, work item card
50: Concept:   Position     → implementations:  column membership (+ optional completion
51:             as state                       flag, archive move, in-column ordering)
52: ```
53: 
54: A reader who has only seen one product's vocabulary should still recognize any other board tool from this model.
55: 
56: ### Standard Capabilities
57: 
58: Mature products almost universally add:
59: 
60: - **Card detail** — description, assignee/members, due dates, labels or colors, attachments, checklists/subtasks, comments with notifications, per-card activity history.
61: - **Real-time collaboration** — several people working the same board with live updates.
62: - **Board membership and permissions** — who can see or edit a board; role tiers on larger accounts; per-board access levels.
63: - **Workflow customization** — rename/add/reorder columns, sub-columns, collapsible columns and swimlanes, board backgrounds.
64: - **Search and filtering** — find cards across the board (and the archive) by text, member, label, date.
65: - **Board templates and cloning** — start from a prebuilt flow (task tracking, sales pipeline, product development) or duplicate an existing board.
66: - **Automation** — rules that move, label, or otherwise act on cards when triggers occur (e.g., "when a card moves to review, assign a reviewer").
67: - **Archiving** — completed cards leave the board but remain searchable.
68: - **Notifications** — assignments, mentions, and due-date reminders, typically via email or in-app.
69: - **API, integrations, and mobile clients.**
70: 
71: ### Optional / Segment-dependent Capabilities
72: 
73: - **WIP limits** — a cap per column on how many cards it may hold, so the team finishes started work before pulling more. Method-standard for kanban practice and prominent in methodology-first products; not present natively in every general-purpose tool.
74: - **Swimlanes** — present in many team-oriented products, absent from the simplest forms.
75: - **Flow analytics** — cumulative flow diagrams, cycle/lead time, aging, forecasting from historical data. The signature of methodology-first and enterprise offerings.
76: - **Time tracking** — timers and reports attached to cards (a differentiator of some products rather than the norm).
77: - **Secondary views** — calendar, timeline, table, or dashboard renderings of the same cards.
78: - **Cross-board machinery** — moving cards between boards, linked board networks, portfolio layers above boards in enterprise suites.
79: - **AI assistance** — text drafting, board construction from a description, or agents that execute cards on the board (current-generation layer).
80: 
81: ## How It Works
82: 
83: ### Shape the board
84: 
85: ```text
86: Create a board
87: → name the columns after the real process (often starting from a template:
88:    "to do / doing / done", or a richer request → in progress → review → done)
89: → optionally split columns, add swimlanes, set WIP limits
90: → invite members, set who can view/edit
91: ```
92: 
93: The board is configured, not programmed. As the process changes, the columns change — the same vendor guidance everywhere: the board should mirror how the team actually works.
94: 
95: ### Fill and work the flow
96: 
97: ```text
98: Cards enter the board (added by hand, captured from requests/integrations,
99:    or imported in bulk)
100: → a member picks up a card (usually from the top of the first column)
101: → moves it into the working column
102: → does the work; discusses and attaches material on the card
103: → moves it onward through review/delivery stages
104: → it reaches done and is archived or left to rest
105: ```
106: 
107: This is a pull loop: people take up work as they free themselves, ideally finishing what they have before starting more. Where WIP limits are configured, the overfilled column becomes visible as a stop signal; how strictly the software enforces the cap varies by product. Dragging the card is not decoration — it *is* the status update, performed by the person doing the work, which is why the board can stay current without a reporting ceremony.
108: 
109: ### Steer by looking
110: 
111: The board is designed to be read at a distance: a glance shows what is on deck, what is in motion, what is done, and where cards accumulate. Teams use it in their regular check-ins; bottlenecks show up as fat columns, stalled or blocked work as aging cards, and overload as columns pressed against their limits. Managers and stakeholders read the same surface instead of asking for status.
112: 
113: ### Adjust over time
114: 
115: Boards are living structures: columns get renamed, merged, or sliced as the process is refined; cards get moved between boards; finished boards are archived. The improvement loop — look at flow, change the board, work the new flow — is part of the product's normal operation.
116: 
117: ### Defining core vs standard vs optional
118: 
119: - **Defining core** — board, cards, position-as-state, movement as the state change.
120: - **Standard capabilities** — card detail, real-time collaboration, permissions, workflow customization, search/filter, templates, automation, archive, notifications, API/mobile.
121: - **Optional / variant** — WIP limits, swimlanes, flow analytics, time tracking, secondary views, cross-board linking, AI, deployment choices, personal vs team orientation.
122: 
123: ## Interfaces
124: 
125: ### The board surface
126: 
127: The product's main screen.
128: 
129: - shows the board: columns left to right, swimlanes across, cards stacked in each column
130: - cards display a summary face (title, colors/labels, members, due date, checklist progress)
131: - primary actions: add a card, drag a card within or across columns, filter/search, open a card, collapse areas, open the board menu
132: 
133: ### Card detail view
134: 
135: Opens from any card.
136: 
137: - description, checklist with progress, members, dates, labels, attachments, comments, activity history
138: - primary actions: edit details, assign, comment, attach, move (or drag from here), copy/move to another board, archive or delete
139: 
140: ### Board menu / settings
141: 
142: The board's control panel.
143: 
144: - members and permissions, background and appearance, automation rules, power-ups/extensions, activity feed, archive access
145: - primary actions: manage access, configure the workflow (columns, swimlanes, WIP limits), set up automations, search the board
146: 
147: ### Boards home / switcher
148: 
149: The entry surface listing a user's boards and available templates.
150: 
151: - board previews, favorites, team/workspace groupings, template gallery
152: - primary actions: create a board, start from a template, open a recent board
153: 
154: ### Secondary surfaces (where offered)
155: 
156: Calendar, timeline, table, or dashboard renderings of the same cards; analytics screens (cumulative flow, cycle time, aging) in methodology-oriented products.
157: 
158: ## Important Rules / Behaviors
159: 
160: - **Position is the status.** The card's column membership is the authoritative state of the work. There is no second status field to reconcile; the board cannot lie about where work stands unless someone fails to move a card.
161: - **The workflow is user-defined.** The product fixes no particular set of stages. Column names, count, and meaning are the users' own; two boards in the same product can model entirely different processes.
162: - **Movement is the update operation.** Dragging a card between columns — with the position confirmed in the card's history — is how state changes are made; some products let rules automate specific moves.
163: - **Capacity rules bind when configured.** A WIP limit makes an overfull column visually (and sometimes mechanically) resist new cards. The pull discipline — finish before starting more — is a practice the board supports, not one software generally enforces.
164: - **Card order carries sequence.** Within a column, top-to-bottom order serves as the working priority, and members commonly take up cards from the top.
165: - **Terminal work is preserved, not erased.** Completion moves cards to a done state or an archive; history remains inspectable, and the archive is searchable.
166: - **Access is scoped per board.** A board has its own member/permission scope; boards can be private, team-shared, or broadly visible depending on the product's model.
167: - **Boards are cheap to create and disposable by design.** One process or purpose per board; proliferation is expected and handled with a home/switcher surface.
168: 
169: ## Variants
170: 
171: - **Personal kanban boards** — single-user boards for private to-dos and planning; the simplest full form of the Type.
172: - **Team process boards** — shared boards with permissions, swimlanes, and automation; the center of gravity of the market.
173: - **General-purpose board-first tools** — the archetype: any workflow, any purpose, boards as the whole product.
174: - **Methodology-first products** — lean/kanban-practice tools that foreground WIP limits, explicit policies, and flow metrics.
175: - **Boards as a module** — board functionality embedded in task-management, workspace, or project-portfolio suites; the board's own model is unchanged by the packaging.
176: - **Enterprise deployments** — linked board networks, portfolio layers above boards, enterprise access governance.
177: - **Deployment forms** — cloud service, self-hosted commercial, open-source self-hosted.
178: - **Secondary board uses** — idea boards, information and resource hubs: the same surface applied where the "flow" degenerates to loose categories.
179: 
180: ## Related Application Types
181: 
182: | Application Type | Distinction |
183: |---|---|
184: | To-do List Application | centers on a flat checklist with completion ticks and reminders; no board grammar — remove the columns and position-as-state and this Type collapses into it |
185: | Task Management Application | centers on task *records* with status fields, priority, and list/calendar views; a kanban board there is one projection view over the records, whereas here the board is the native model and position is the state of record — the sharpest seam in this cluster |
186: | Agile Project Management Application | the board is one surface of that Type; its defining structure adds a team-owned ordered backlog, a bounded delivery cadence (timeboxed iteration or continuous pull) as the re-planning boundary, and feedback metrics — none of which belongs to this Type's core |
187: | Project Management Application | plan/schedule-centric: tasks with dates, dependencies, and resources measured against a plan; a board may be one of its views |
188: | Digital Whiteboard | a freeform spatial canvas with no card-state model; kanban templates on a whiteboard are optional task machinery, not this Type — remove position-as-state and allow free arrangement and it becomes a whiteboard |
189: | Issue Tracker / Bug Tracking System | centers on the issue record and its admin-defined workflow schema and reporting; boards are a common view rather than the model of record |
190: | Sales Pipeline Management | identical board grammar applied to a different world model (deals, buyers, values, win/loss) — sharing a surface grammar does not make one Type |
191: | Work Management / Team Workspace Platforms | broad containers that may include boards as one module; embedding is packaging, not Type identity |
192: 
193: The boundary worth remembering: the question is never "does the product have a kanban view?" but "is the board where the work state lives?" If the board is a rendering over a task table, the product belongs to task management; if the board is the record, it is a Kanban Task Board.
194: 
195: ## Representative Products
196: 
197: - Trello — general-purpose board-first archetype (personal free tier through enterprise)
198: - Kanban Tool — SMB/team pure-play with kanban-method emphasis and time tracking
199: - Businessmap (formerly Kanbanize) — enterprise lean platform carrying boards inside a portfolio/OKR suite
200: - Wekan — open-source, self-hosted board tool
201:

{
  "authored": {
    "name": "Personal Project Board (个人小项目看板) - local single-user kanban board",
    "audience": "One person running a small personal project on their own machine (the board's only user), plus the engineer who implements and probes it. The user names the board, names the columns after their own workflow, writes cards with a title and a short description, moves cards between and inside columns, and reopens the app expecting the same board, column order and card order. The implementer needs an exact, dependency-free local contract they can code and assert against.",
    "objective": "Deliver a localhost-only, single-user, Python-stdlib web application that persists named boards, user-named ordered columns and ordered cards (title + short description) in one SQLite file, treats a card's column membership as the card's state (no separate status field), supports column add/rename/reorder and card move/reorder, shows every column's full card list with per-column counts, and reads the whole structure back unchanged after a restart. P0 explicitly excludes accounts, collaboration, a separate status field, WIP limits, notifications, time reports and automation, and those concepts are rejected at the API boundary rather than merely omitted.",
    "workflow": [
      "1. Operator starts the process with `python3 app.py --data-dir ./data --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765`; the data directory and the SQLite file are created on first run and the startup banner prints the local URL.",
      "2. The user opens `GET /` (boards home) and creates a named board, optionally seeding user-named columns (for example 待办 / 进行中 / 完成) in one step; the board is stored with zero hidden default columns.",
      "3. The user adds further columns, renames a column in place, and reorders columns to match the real workflow; the column order is stored as a contiguous 1..N position sequence and is always rendered left to right.",
      "4. The user creates a card with a title and a short description inside a chosen column; the card is appended at the bottom of that column unless an explicit slot is given.",
      "5. The user edits a card's title or description; editing never changes the card's column, position or moved timestamp.",
      "6. The user moves a card to another column (this is the state change - there is no status field) and reorders cards inside a column; the source column and target column are renumbered to contiguous 1..N in one transaction.",
      "7. The user reads the board surface: columns left to right, each column showing its full ordered card list and its card count, with the board total equal to the sum of the column counts.",
      "8. The user restarts the process against the same `--data-dir` and sees the same boards, the same column order and the same card order, because every write is committed to `<data-dir>/kanban.sqlite3`.",
      "9. The acceptance probe (one disposable board per case, deleting only what it created) exercises the same journey over the JSON API and asserts the zero-write behaviour of every rejected request."
    ],
    "acceptance": [
      "The probe runs against a live target with `python3 probe.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8765 --case A01` (or `--case all`, repeatable `--case` flags) and exits 0 only when every selected case passes; the five cases A01..A05 map one-to-one onto the five features.",
      "A01 proves board behaviour: POST /api/boards creates exactly one board (201 with id, name, created_at, updated_at, column_count, card_count), GET /api/boards grows by exactly one entry and carries the same name and counts, GET /api/boards/{id} returns the same board with an empty column list, PATCH renames without changing the id, and DELETE removes exactly that board.",
      "A02 proves column behaviour: seeded columns keep their names and order with positions 1..3, a new column is appended at position 4, a rename keeps the position, a reorder persists the new order with positions exactly 1..4 and names still attached to the same ids, and deleting an empty column renumbers the remaining columns to 1..N.",
      "A03 proves card behaviour: a card is created with title, description, column and position 1, a second card gets position 2, the board's card_count and the per-column card_count equal the real number of cards, and PATCH changes only title/description (position, column and moved_at unchanged).",
      "Every rejected request in A01..A04 is followed by a re-read that proves zero writes: the board/column/card counts, the column order, the card order, the card positions and each card's updated_at are byte-for-byte the same before and after the rejection (board_state() comparison).",
      "Negative cases are exact: blank or over-long name, blank or over-long title, over-long description, missing column, unknown column (404 COLUMN_NOT_FOUND), a column of another board (422 COLUMN_BOARD_MISMATCH), position 0 or position beyond the last slot (422 POSITION_OUT_OF_RANGE), duplicate column name (409 DUPLICATE_COLUMN_NAME), deleting a non-empty column (409 COLUMN_NOT_EMPTY), deleting the last column (409 LAST_COLUMN), malformed JSON body (400 MALFORMED_JSON), and forbidden P0 keys such as status, assignee, due_date, recurrence_trigger, task_limit (422 FORBIDDEN_FIELD) or colour (422 UNKNOWN_FIELD).",
      "A04 proves position-as-state: moving a card to another column renumbers the source column to 1..M-1 and the target column to 1..N, an in-column reorder swaps the two cards and their positions, the board's total card count is unchanged by every move, moved_at never precedes created_at, and a no-op move leaves the column order untouched.",
      "A05 proves the read model and the date edges: GET /api/boards/{id} returns the columns in position order, each with its full ordered card list, a card_count equal to the length of that list, contiguous card positions starting at 1, a board card_count equal to the sum of the column counts, the expected exact set of card titles per column, an identical snapshot on a second read, and created_at <= updated_at and created_at <= moved_at for every card inside the probe's write window.",
      "Cross-process restart durability is specified in README.md as an operator procedure (stop the process, start it again with the same --data-dir, re-read the board) because the probe cannot stop or start the server; the blueprint claims that step was not executed, and the whole runtime verification of this target is not_run.",
      "The probe only uses records it created in its own disposable board and deletes only those records; it never deletes pre-existing user data, and it asserts only behaviour documented in this architecture - no upstream Kanboard behaviour is asserted."
    ],
    "observations": [
      ["documentation", "README.md", 4, 14, "Upstream README describes Kanboard as project management software that focuses on the Kanban methodology and states the application is in maintenance mode: the author is not actively developing any new major features, only small fixes are made, and pull requests for new features and bug fixes are accepted."],
      ["documentation", "README.md", 19, 27, "Upstream README links the official website, a feature list, the change log, a forum and the documentation pages for requirements, installation, upgrade and Docker use, i.e. upstream is a full server product with its own documentation and deployment story, not a local single-user tool."],
      ["documentation", "README.md", 29, 34, "Upstream README names Frederic Guillot as main developer, points at the contributor list and states that the project is distributed under the MIT License."],
      ["documentation", "LICENSE", 1, 21, "The pinned upstream LICENSE is the MIT License (MIT), copyright (c) Frederic Guillot, with the standard grant, the notice requirement and the warranty disclaimer."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Model/ColumnModel.php", 183, 195, "Upstream create() persists a new column for a project with title, task_limit (a WIP cap), description and hide_in_dashboard, and sets position to getLastColumnPosition(project_id) + 1, so a newly added column is appended at the end of the board rather than inserted at an arbitrary slot."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Model/ColumnModel.php", 208, 216, "Upstream update() rewrites the column title, task_limit, hide_in_dashboard and description in place and never touches the column position, so renaming a column is independent of the column order."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Model/ColumnModel.php", 239, 261, "Upstream changePosition() rejects a position below 1 or above the number of columns of the project, then renumbers the sibling columns ascending by their current position and finally writes the requested position on the moved column, returning false if any single update fails - reordering is a bounded, all-or-nothing rewrite of the sibling positions."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Model/ColumnModel.php", 118, 121, "Upstream getAll() returns the columns of a project ordered ascending by position, which is the mechanism behind the left-to-right column order of the board surface."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Model/ColumnModel.php", 147, 156, "Upstream getAllWithTaskCount() returns the columns ordered by position together with a per-column count of open tasks (is_active='1') and of closed tasks (is_active='0'), i.e. upstream derives the column card counts from the task table itself."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Model/ColumnModel.php", 225, 228, "Upstream remove() deletes a column row by id and its docblock states that the column and all associated tasks are removed, so upstream column deletion is destructive rather than a move of the cards elsewhere."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Model/TaskPositionModel.php", 66, 97, "Upstream movePosition() returns false for a position below 1, resolves the swimlane when none is given, skips closed tasks when onlyOpen is set, and then dispatches to exactly one of three branches - swimlane change, column change or same-column position change - so a card's placement is the only way its location changes."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Model/TaskPositionModel.php", 177, 215, "Upstream saveTaskPositions() lists the other tasks of the same column ordered by position then id, inserts the moved task when the requested position equals the running offset, rewrites every other task's position, and finally places the task at the bottom while normalising a bad position - the whole column is renumbered around the moved card."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Model/TaskPositionModel.php", 112, 121, "Upstream saveSwimlaneChange() performs the source-column rewrite, the target-column rewrite and the timestamp update inside one database transaction and returns the conjunction of the three results, i.e. a move commits as a single all-or-nothing unit."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Model/TaskPositionModel.php", 135, 144, "Upstream saveColumnChange() applies the same transaction pattern for a move between two columns: clear the source column, fill the target column, update the timestamps, and report success only when all three writes succeeded."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Model/TaskPositionModel.php", 244, 258, "Upstream saveTaskPosition() cancels the surrounding transaction when the row update affects no rows, which is how a failed mid-move write aborts the whole move instead of leaving a half-renumbered column."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Model/TaskPositionModel.php", 15, 51, "Upstream moveBottom() computes MAX(position)+1 over the tasks of the target column and writes column_id, position, date_moved and date_modification, so appending a card to a column is a position write and not a separate status flag."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Model/TaskPositionModel.php", 269, 313, "Upstream fireEvents() emits a distinct event for a swimlane change, a column change or a position change and carries src_column_id, dst_column_id, date_moved and the task's recurrence fields; in upstream the move is the state-change event of the card."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Model/TaskCreationModel.php", 61, 93, "Upstream prepare() defaults an empty column_id to the first column of the project, defaults an empty title to 'Untitled', stamps date_creation, date_modification and date_moved with the current time and computes position as the number of tasks in the column plus one."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Model/TaskCreationModel.php", 22, 53, "Upstream create() persists the task row first and only afterwards calls movePosition() when an explicit position greater than one was requested, i.e. inserting a card at a chosen slot is a create step followed by a position step."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Model/TaskModificationModel.php", 23, 41, "Upstream update() applies the changed fields to the task row and fires the modification events only when the write succeeded; the card's text fields are edited independently of its column and position."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Model/TaskModificationModel.php", 105, 117, "Upstream prepare() converts date_due and date_started through the date parser, removes the id field, resets the date, score and time fields and stamps date_modification - upstream tasks carry due/start dates and recurrence counters, which the pinned P0 scenario deliberately excludes."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Controller/TaskMovePositionController.php", 33, 52, "Upstream TaskMovePositionController::save() reads a JSON body with column_id, position and swimlane_id, checks a move permission on the project role, calls movePosition() with the project id, the task id and those three values, and then redirects back to the task view."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Template/board/table_column.php", 5, 27, "The upstream board template renders one table header cell per column carrying data-column-id, the escaped column title and a per-column dropdown, so the column order of the board surface is exactly the column position order."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Template/board/table_column.php", 88, 120, "The upstream column header renders the score, the visible task count and - when a task_limit is set - the total across swimlanes, i.e. upstream already shows a per-column card count next to the column title."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Template/board/table_column.php", 105, 119, "The upstream task count block is rendered only when the count is non-empty and is preceded by an ui-helper-hidden-accessible 'Task count' text, i.e. upstream labels the column count for assistive technology."],
      ["code_observation", "app/Template/board/table_column.php", 39, 43, "The upstream column dropdown offers 'Close all tasks in this column and this swimlane' only when the column holds tasks, showing that upstream treats the column as the container whose content can be closed in bulk - a batch operation outside the pinned P0 scenario."]
    ],
    "inference": "Evidence classes are kept separate. (1) code_observation = behaviour read directly from the pinned upstream files at the cited lines (for example upstream renumbers a column around a moved card inside one transaction, upstream bounds a column reorder by the number of columns, upstream renders a per-column task count). (2) documentation = claims read from upstream README.md and LICENSE and from leaf.md; leaf.md describes the Kanban Task Board type in general terms and explicitly separates the defining core (board, card, position-as-state) from standard and optional capabilities. (3) target design inference = every statement about the local Python/SQLite target in this blueprint, including the data model, the API surface, the validation bounds, the error codes, the UI and the probe, is my own design derived from the pinned scenario plus the leaf's defining core; it is not an upstream capability and upstream code was not copied. (4) not_run upstream status = the pinned Kanboard snapshot was read as text only; it was never installed, started or exercised, so no upstream runtime behaviour, upstream database schema or upstream performance figure is asserted anywhere here. The target's own runtime verification is likewise not_run: no server was started and no probe case was executed while writing this blueprint. Upstream-only concepts visible in the evidence (swimlanes, task_limit as a WIP cap, tags, score, priority, recurrence counters, bulk creation, project-role permissions, markdown tooltips) were read as evidence of the category's standard capabilities and are deliberately kept out of the target P0; the target rejects them at the API boundary instead of ignoring them.",
    "features": [
      "Named boards with durable local storage (create, list, read, rename, delete)",
      "User-named ordered columns (add, rename, reorder, guarded delete)",
      "Cards with a title and a short description (create, read, edit)",
      "Movement as state: cross-column move and in-column reorder with contiguous renumbering",

    "goals": [
      "A POST /api/boards with a 1..120 character name creates exactly one board row and answers 201 with id, name, created_at, updated_at, column_count and card_count; GET /api/boards then lists that board once with the same counts, GET /api/boards/{id} returns the same board with an empty column list, and after the process is restarted with the same --data-dir the same board id, name and counts are read back unchanged.",
      "Columns can be appended, renamed in place and reordered: after every accepted change the board's columns are exactly the contiguous permutation 1..N of their positions, GET /api/boards/{id} returns them in that order with every name still attached to the same column id, deleting an empty column renumbers the remaining columns to 1..N, and deleting a non-empty column (409 COLUMN_NOT_EMPTY) or the last column of a board (409 LAST_COLUMN) is rejected without writing.",
      "A card can be created in a chosen column with a required title of 1..200 characters and an optional description of at most 500 characters, is appended at the bottom of that column unless an explicit slot is requested, and PATCH can change only the title and the description - never the column, the position or moved_at; a rejected card write (blank or over-long title, over-long description, missing or unknown column, forbidden key such as status, due_date or recurrence_trigger, unknown key such as colour) leaves the card set, the card order, the per-column counts and every card's updated_at exactly unchanged.",
      "POST /api/cards/{id}/move with (column_id, position) places the card in the 1-based slot position of the target column, renumbers the source column to 1..M-1 and the target column to 1..N inside one transaction, keeps the board's total card count unchanged and bumps moved_at, while an out-of-range position, an unknown column, a column belonging to another board and an unknown card are all rejected without any write.",
      "GET /api/boards/{id} returns the board, its columns in position order and for every column the complete ordered list of its cards plus a card_count equal to the length of that list, so that the column counts sum to the board card_count, every card list carries contiguous positions starting at 1, the expected card titles appear exactly in the expected columns, and two consecutive reads return an identical snapshot."
    ],
    "arch": "# Architecture - Personal Project Board (个人小项目看板)\n\n## 1. Scope and non-goals\nP0 scope: one local, single-user process that stores named boards; every board holds user-named columns in a user-defined order; every column holds ordered cards; a card carries a title and a short description; a card's column membership IS its state; column order and card order are persisted and shown; the whole structure is read back unchanged after a restart.\n\nRejected at the API boundary (422 FORBIDDEN_FIELD) and absent from the schema: accounts and login, roles and permissions, multi-user collaboration, a separate status/state field, WIP limits, swimlanes, due/start dates, recurrence, notifications, time tracking and reports, automation, templates, search/filter, archive, secondary views, external integrations.\n\n## 2. Runtime, files and start instructions\n- Python 3.9+, standard library only (http.server, sqlite3, json, urllib.parse, argparse).\n- Start: `python3 app.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765 --data-dir ./data`\n  - `--host` default 127.0.0.1 (loopback only), `--port` default 8765, `--data-dir` default ./data.\n  - Env override: `PERSONAL_KANBAN_DATA_DIR`.\n  - Startup order: create the data directory if missing; open `<data-dir>/kanban.sqlite3`; apply the schema with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` (PRAGMA user_version = 1); `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`, `PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000`; print `Personal Project Board listening on http://127.0.0.1:8765/`.\n  - Shutdown: SIGINT / Ctrl-C closes the connection and checkpoints the WAL; committed data is not lost.\n- Target file layout: `app.py`, `personal_board/db.py` (schema and connection), `personal_board/service.py` (transactional domain logic), `personal_board/api.py` (JSON endpoints), `personal_board/web.py` (HTML endpoints), `personal_board/server.py` (router), `probe.py`, `README.md`.\n- Storage: exactly one SQLite file `<data-dir>/kanban.sqlite3` (plus `-wal` / `-shm` sidecars). No other state is kept in memory across restarts.\n- No authentication and no TLS: the process binds loopback only and is single-user (decision D1).\n\n## 3. Data model (SQLite, one file, PRAGMA user_version = 1)\nboards\n  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT\n  name        TEXT    NOT NULL   -- trimmed, 1..120 chars\n  created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL   -- UTC epoch seconds\n  updated_at  INTEGER NOT NULL\n\ncolumns\n  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT\n  board_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES boards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE\n  name        TEXT    NOT NULL   -- trimmed, 1..120 chars, unique per board (case-insensitive)\n  position    INTEGER NOT NULL   -- 1..N inside the board\n  created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL\n  updated_at  INTEGER NOT NULL\n  UNIQUE (board_id, position)\n\ncards\n  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT\n  board_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES boards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE\n  column_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES columns(id) ON DELETE CASCADE\n  position    INTEGER NOT NULL   -- 1..N inside the column\n  title       TEXT    NOT NULL   -- trimmed, 1..200 chars\n  description TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT ''   -- 0..500 chars\n  created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL\n  updated_at  INTEGER NOT NULL\n  moved_at    INTEGER NOT NULL   -- last time the card changed column or position\n  UNIQUE (column_id, position)\n\nInvariants after every committed write:\n- the columns of a board form exactly the permutation 1..N of their positions;\n- the cards of a column form exactly the permutation 1..N of their positions;\n- a card's board_id always equals the board_id of its column;\n- no status, state, priority, assignee, date or recurrence column exists anywhere.\n\n## 4. HTTP API (JSON, UTF-8, Content-Type application/json)\nError envelope for every non-2xx answer:\n  {\"error\": {\"code\": \"POSITION_OUT_OF_RANGE\", \"message\": \"position must be between 1 and 3\", \"field\": \"position\", \"details\": {\"min\": 1, \"max\": 3}}}\n\nHealth\n  GET /api/health -> 200 {\"status\": \"ok\", \"schema_version\": 1, \"data_dir\": \"/abs/path\"}\n\nBoards\n  GET /api/boards -> 200 {\"boards\": [{\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"Home\", \"created_at\": 1760000000, \"updated_at\": 1760000000, \"column_count\": 3, \"card_count\": 4}]}\n  POST /api/boards\n    request  {\"name\": \"Home\", \"columns\": [\"待办\", \"进行中\"]}   # name required, columns optional\n    response 201 {\"board\": {\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"Home\", \"created_at\": ..., \"updated_at\": ..., \"column_count\": 2, \"card_count\": 0},\n                   \"columns\": [{\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"待办\", \"position\": 1, \"card_count\": 0, \"created_at\": ..., \"updated_at\": ...}]}\n  GET /api/boards/{board_id} -> 200\n    {\"board\": {\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"Home\", \"created_at\": ..., \"updated_at\": ..., \"column_count\": 2, \"card_count\": 3},\n     \"columns\": [{\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"待办\", \"position\": 1, \"card_count\": 2,\n                  \"cards\": [{\"id\": 11, \"board_id\": 1, \"column_id\": 1, \"position\": 1, \"title\": \"...\", \"description\": \"...\",\n                             \"created_at\": ..., \"updated_at\": ..., \"moved_at\": ...}]}]}\n  PATCH /api/boards/{board_id} request {\"name\": \"...\"} -> 200 {\"board\": {...}}\n  DELETE /api/boards/{board_id} -> 204 (cascades to that board's columns and cards)\n\nColumns\n  POST /api/boards/{board_id}/columns request {\"name\": \"...\"} -> 201 {\"column\": {\"id\": 3, \"board_id\": 1, \"name\": \"...\", \"position\": 3, \"card_count\": 0, \"created_at\": ..., \"updated_at\": ...}}\n  GET /api/columns/{column_id} -> 200 {\"column\": {...}}\n  PATCH /api/columns/{column_id} request {\"name\": \"...\"} -> 200 {\"column\": {...}}\n  PUT /api/columns/{column_id}/position request {\"position\": 2} -> 200\n    {\"column\": {...}, \"columns\": [{\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"待办\", \"position\": 1}, {\"id\": 3, \"name\": \"完成\", \"position\": 2}]}\n  DELETE /api/columns/{column_id} -> 204 | 409 COLUMN_NOT_EMPTY | 409 LAST_COLUMN\n\nCards\n  POST /api/boards/{board_id}/cards\n    request  {\"title\": \"...\", \"description\": \"...\", \"column_id\": 1, \"position\": 2}\n             # title and column_id required; description optional (default \"\"); position optional (default: append at the bottom)\n    response 201 {\"card\": {\"id\": 11, \"board_id\": 1, \"column_id\": 1, \"position\": 2, \"title\": \"...\", \"description\": \"...\", \"created_at\": ..., \"updated_at\": ..., \"moved_at\": ...}}\n  GET /api/cards/{card_id} -> 200 {\"card\": {...}}\n  PATCH /api/cards/{card_id} request {\"title\": \"...\", \"description\": \"...\"} -> 200 {\"card\": {...}}\n  POST /api/cards/{card_id}/move request {\"column_id\": 2, \"position\": 1} -> 200\n    {\"card\": {...},\n     \"columns\": [{\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"待办\", \"position\": 1, \"card_count\": 1, \"card_ids\": [12]},\n                 {\"id\": 2, \"name\": \"进行中\", \"position\": 2, \"card_count\": 2, \"card_ids\": [11, 13]}]}\n  DELETE /api/cards/{card_id} -> 204\n\n## 5. Validation bounds, allowed keys and error codes\nField bounds\n  board.name          trimmed, 1..120 chars            -> 422 NAME_REQUIRED / NAME_TOO_LONG\n  column.name         trimmed, 1..120 chars            -> 422 NAME_REQUIRED / NAME_TOO_LONG\n  column.name         unique per board, case-insensitive-> 409 DUPLICATE_COLUMN_NAME\n  card.title          trimmed, 1..200 chars            -> 422 TITLE_REQUIRED / TITLE_TOO_LONG\n  card.description    0..500 chars, default \"\"        -> 422 DESCRIPTION_TOO_LONG\n  card.column_id      required on create               -> 422 COLUMN_REQUIRED\n                      must exist                       -> 404 COLUMN_NOT_FOUND\n                      must belong to the board in the path -> 422 COLUMN_BOARD_MISMATCH\n  card.position       optional on create, 1..(count+1) -> 422 POSITION_OUT_OF_RANGE\n  move.position       1..(target count after removal + 1) -> 422 POSITION_OUT_OF_RANGE\n  column.position     1..number of columns of the board-> 422 POSITION_OUT_OF_RANGE\n\nAllowed request keys (any other key is rejected)\n  POST /api/boards                 name, columns\n  PATCH /api/boards/{id}           name\n  POST /api/boards/{id}/columns    name\n  PATCH /api/columns/{id}          name\n  PUT  /api/columns/{id}/position   position\n  POST /api/boards/{id}/cards      title, description, column_id, position\n  PATCH /api/cards/{id}            title, description\n  POST /api/cards/{id}/move        column_id, position\n\nForbidden keys (P0 guard, checked before any write) -> 422 FORBIDDEN_FIELD:\n  status, state, workflow_status, is_active, closed, completed, archived,\n  assignee, owner, owner_id, member, members, priority, score, tags, tag, label, labels,\n  color, color_id, due_date, date_due, start_date, date_started, deadline, end_date,\n  recurrence, recurrence_status, recurrence_trigger, recurrence_factor, recurrence_timeframe,\n  recurrence_basedate, repeat, every, remind, reminder, notification, notifications, notify,\n  wip_limit, task_limit, limit, swimlane, swimlane_id, time_estimated, time_spent, duration,\n  estimate, checklist, checklists, comment, comments, attachment, attachments, subtask, subtasks,\n  template, templates, rule, rules, automation, external_id, external_provider, email, password,\n  username, role, roles, permission, permissions, created_at, updated_at, moved_at\n  Any other unknown key -> 422 UNKNOWN_FIELD.\n  column_id inside PATCH /api/cards/{id} -> 422 COLUMN_CHANGE_REQUIRES_MOVE.\n  position inside PATCH /api/cards/{id} -> 422 POSITION_CHANGE_REQUIRES_MOVE.\n\nHTTP status codes\n  200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 303 See Other (UI redirect),\n  400 MALFORMED_JSON (body is not valid JSON) / 400 INVALID_BODY (body is not a JSON object),\n  404 NOT_FOUND (unknown route), 404 BOARD_NOT_FOUND, 404 COLUMN_NOT_FOUND, 404 CARD_NOT_FOUND,\n  405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED (with an Allow header),\n  409 DUPLICATE_COLUMN_NAME, 409
